g.text: This is what might end up happening if you were to run great in dissent, ​if you

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: were to use your training data as is. ​Because the contours are so tall and

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: ​skinny gradient descent may end up bouncing back and forth for ​a long time

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: before it can finally find its way to the global minimum.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: In situations like this, a useful thing to do is to scale the features.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: ​This means performing some transformation of your training data so ​that x1 say might now range from 0 to 1 and x2

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: might also range from 0 to 1. ​So the data points now look more like this and you might notice that the scale of ​the plot

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: on the bottom is now quite different than the one on top.
